newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso battered at close by speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso battered at close by speculation.

text.p: The Mexican peso sharply swiftly extended earlier softness at the close of trade on Monday due to a speculative onslaught triggered by a cocktail of month-end demand for dollars and jitters ahead of key U.S. data, traders said.
"U.S. data this week do not look at all good, and that really squeezed the market," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 8.4 and 7.7 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9700/7.9800 and 7.9600/7.9700 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 3.7 centavos weaker at 7.9170/7.9200 per dollar.
Traders said they would look very carefully at the effect on the U.S. bond market of U.S. first quarter GDP and employment data due this week.
"I don't know where the peso will go in the coming days. There was much speculation today, particularly by one local bank that spent the whole session buying dollars," a trader said.
Dealers said primary rates could increase at Banco de Mexico's primary auction later in the day in response to a weaker peso.

Nonetheless, money market traders surveyed by Reuters said they forecast the central bank would assign bellwether 29-day Cetes at an average of 20.00 percent. This would be a fall of 23 basis points since last week's auction.
The central bank moved forward its weekly auction of government securities as the business week will be shortened by a public holiday on Thursday, May 1, to celebrate Labor Day.
Banco de Mexico is due to announce the results of its auction at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
Dealers situated support for the 48-hour peso at 8.01 per dollar.
